_comment: GEPA seed population. delim and the block shape are the p2o/blocks.json method (strict suffix behind a fixed delimiter). c000 is block A of P2O wave 0 VERBATIM -- the only block with a confirmed paired lift (+0.144 [+0.096, +0.194] on dev120, 2026-09-13). c001-c003 are written seeds, each targeting one behaviour the wave-0 traces showed the model missing. The control arm is not a block: gepa_tree.py adds it as -pctl with an untouched instruction.md.

blocks.c000:
Make every source change with a short Python script: read the file, replace one exact string that occurs exactly once
with the new text, write the file back, and exit non-zero if the string is missing or not unique. Do not use sed -i,
patch, or heredocs for multi-line edits. After each edit, run the language's syntax check on the file (for Python:
python -m py_compile FILE) and print git diff, and read the diff before doing anything else. If an edit went wrong,
restore the file with git checkout -- FILE and redo the whole edit in one step instead of repairing it piece by piece.
blocks.c001:
Before you declare the task complete, re-read the request and write down, in one sentence, what it says the finished
state should be. Then check that state from the outside: run a small script that exercises the behaviour the request
describes and prints the value it asks for, and read the output. Re-reading your own edit is not a check; the check
has to observe the behaviour. If the observed value is not the one the request states, you are not done, whatever the
code looks like. If you cannot build such a check, say so in your analysis and keep working rather than declaring
complete. Never declare complete in the same turn as your last edit.
blocks.c002:
Send a small first batch of commands, at most three, and read the screen before sending more. The first batch should
only establish where you are and where the relevant code lives. Long batches spend context on output you had not yet
decided you needed, and they hide which command produced which result. After each batch write one sentence saying
what the output changed about your plan. Give any single hypothesis about the cause a fixed budget of about five
turns: if the output has not confirmed it by then, write down the next most likely cause and test that instead of
gathering more evidence for the first. Never repeat a command whose output you have already seen.
blocks.c003:
Never delete or truncate anything you were given: no removing source files, no emptying the files that check your
work, no recursive delete of a path inside the working tree. If something looks wrong, read it before you change it.
When an edit does not do what you expected, first print the current contents of the region you edited and compare it
with what you intended; most failed edits are a mismatch you can see. Only after you have looked at the actual state
should you restore the file and redo the edit in one step. Restoring blind, or editing again on top of a state you
have not read, is how a small mistake becomes an unrecoverable one. Keep scratch work in a temporary directory
outside the working tree.
